It is: "The key has gone missing somewhere." More simply: "I cannot find the key."
"Jitna ho sake utna jaldi bhej do" ko English mein bolna hai.
It is: "Please send it as soon as possible." You may also say: "Please send it as quickly as you can."
Hotel ki notice mein "Check-out time 11 AM" likha hai. Matlab?
It means you must leave your room by 11 in the morning. After that time, you may have to pay for extra time.
Aur late check-out ke liye kaise poochun?
Ask: "Is late check-out possible?"
Train ticket pe "WL 5" likha hai. Iska matlab?
"WL" means waiting list. The ticket is not confirmed yet. It can be confirmed if other passengers cancel.
Mail mein "FYI" likha tha. Matlab kya hai?
"FYI" means "for your information". The sender is just letting you know. You do not have to reply.
Friend ke message mein "BTW" likha tha. Iska matlab?
"BTW" means "by the way". People use it to add something extra to the chat.
Shaadi ke card pe "RSVP" likha hai. Ye kya hai?
"RSVP" means "please reply". The hosts want to know whether you will come.
Invitation pe "Dress code: smart casual" likha hai. Matlab?
It means neat and comfortable clothes that are not too formal, like a clean shirt and trousers.
Colleague bola "I am swamped." Iska matlab kya hai?
It means "I am very busy". Use it when you have more work than you can easily do.
"Easy come, easy go" ka matlab kya hai? Dost ne ye paise ke baare mein bola.
It means that things you get easily are also lost easily. It is often said when someone gets something and loses it just as fast.
Main bolta hoon "I am doing job in a bank." Kya ye sahi hai?
It is understood, but it is not natural. Say: "I work in a bank." Or: "I have a job at a bank."
Foreigner ne poocha "Where are you from?" Maine bola "My native is Pune." Wo confuse hua.
"Native" used like this is Indian English. Say: "My hometown is Pune." Or: "I am from Pune."
I always say "I am cent per cent sure." My manager smiled. Why?
"Cent per cent" is common in India, but many English speakers say "one hundred percent". Say: "I am one hundred percent sure."
Bade logon ko aur dost ko "baithiye" alag-alag kaise bolun?
To an elder: "Please have a seat." To a friend: "Take a seat." The first sounds more respectful.
Boss aur dost ko promotion ki badhai alag-alag kaise dun?
To your boss: "Congratulations on your promotion, sir." To a friend: "Congrats on the promotion!"
Reply dene mein deri ho gayi. Formal aur casual dono mein sorry kaise bolun?
Formal: "I apologise for the delay in replying." Casual: "Sorry for the late reply!"
Passport office mein bolna hai ki mujhe passport renew karna hai.
Say: "I want to renew my passport."
Aur poochna hai ki kaun se documents chahiye.
Ask: "Which documents do I need?"
Mobile shop pe poochna hai ki is phone ka cover hai kya.
Ask: "Do you have a cover for this phone?"
Aur "dusre colour mein hai?"
Ask: "Do you have it in another colour?"
Aur "thoda sasta wala dikhao"?
Say: "Could you show me a cheaper one?"
Shaadi mein bolna hai "Main dulhe ka bhai hoon." English?
Say: "I am the groom's brother."
Aur "main dulhan ki saheli hoon"?
Say: "I am the bride's friend." The word "friend" is enough, even for a close girl friend.
Gym mein membership ke baare mein jaankari chahiye. Kya bolun?
Say: "I would like some information about membership."
Aur kya ek trial class ho sakti hai?
Ask: "Is a trial class possible?"
Dost ke kutte ko chhuna hai. Dost se kaise poochun?
Ask: "May I touch your dog?" You can also say: "Is it okay to pet your dog?"
Aur poochna hai ki kya wo kaatta hai.
Ask: "Does he bite?" Ask this before you go near him.
Aunty se bolna hai ki ye recipe mujhe sikha dijiye.
Say: "Aunty, could you teach me this recipe, please?" People in India often call elder women "Aunty", and it is understood in English too.
Aur poochna hai ki kitna namak daalna hai.
Ask: "How much salt should I add?"
Please correct: "Where you are going?"
The correct sentence is: "Where are you going?"
Cafe mein Wi-Fi ka password poochna hai. Kaise bolun?
Say: "Excuse me, could you tell me the Wi-Fi password, please?" This is polite and works in any cafe or shop.
Lift mein koi andar aa raha hai, mujhe door hold karna hai. English mein kya bolun?
Say: "Please come in, I'm holding the door." If the person is far away, you can call out: "Hold on, I'll keep the door open."
Kisi ajnabi se photo khichwani hai. Kaise bolun?
Say: "Excuse me, could you take my photo, please?" When you get the phone back, say: "Thank you so much."
Watchman bhaiya se bolna hai ki gate khol do, mehmaan aane wale hain.
Say: "Please open the gate. Our guests are about to arrive." "About to arrive" means they will be here very soon.
"Beta, jaate waqt darwaza band kar dena." Iska English kya hoga?
It is: "Please close the door when you leave." If you want to keep the loving tone of "beta", you can begin with "Dear," as in "Dear, please close the door when you leave."
I am having two brothers. Is this right?
No. The correct sentence is: "I have two brothers." Why: "have" meaning possession is not used in a continuous form.
Maine kaha "I passed out of college in 2015." Ek foreigner hans pada. Kyun?
In many countries "pass out" means to faint, so he may have pictured you fainting. To say you finished your studies, say: "I graduated from college in 2015."
"Kya main aapka phone use kar sakta hoon?" polite aur casual dono mein bataiye.
Polite: "May I use your phone, please?" Casual: "Can I use your phone for a second?" Use the first with elders or strangers and the second with friends.
"Jab main chhota tha, tab hum gaon mein rehte the." English mein kya hoga?
It is: "When I was small, we lived in a village."
Isme "used to live" bhi chalega kya?
Yes. "We used to live in a village" is also correct. It shows that this was true in the past but is not true now.
Bachche ko aaj school se jaldi lena hai. Teacher ko kaise bataun?
Say: "I need to pick up my child early today. Is that all right?" You can add the time you will arrive if you know it.
Mere ghar mein sab bolte hain "open the light". Kya ye sahi hai?
No. In standard English we say "turn on the light" or "switch on the light", and "turn off" or "switch off" to stop it. "Open" is used for things like doors, windows and boxes.
Aur fan ke liye?
The same rule works: "Please turn on the fan" and "Please turn off the fan."
Ghar aaye mehmaan ko bolna hai "Aap baithiye, main chai laati hoon." English?
Say: "Please have a seat. I will bring you some tea." "Have a seat" is a friendly, polite way to say "sit down".
"Aaj mera office mein pehla din hai." Ise English mein likho.
It is: "Today is my first day at the office."
I bought a umbrella yesterday. Correct it, is it fine?
No. The correct sentence is: "I bought an umbrella yesterday." Why: "umbrella" begins with a vowel sound, so we use "an", not "a".
Boss ne bola "Let's prepone the meeting." Ye proper English hai kya?
"Prepone" is widely used in India, but many English speakers outside India will not know it. A clearer way to say it is: "Let's move the meeting earlier."
Samajh nahi aaya to "Thoda saaf bolo" polite aur casual mein kaise bolun?
Polite: "Could you speak more clearly, please? I did not understand." Casual: "Sorry, I didn't get that. Can you say it more clearly?"
Paani ki bottle refill karwani hai. Kisi se kaise bolun?
Say: "Could you please refill my water bottle?" If you are at home, "Can you fill this up for me?" also works.
"Maine cheezein bag mein rakh di hain." Translate karo.
It is: "I have put the things in the bag." You can also say "I've put everything in the bag."
I am go to school by bus every day. Please fix.
The correct sentence is: "I go to school by bus every day." Why: "am" belongs with an -ing form and cannot go with "go"; a daily routine uses the simple present.
To "I am going to school" kab bolte hain?
We use it for something happening now, or planned soon, such as "I am going to school now."
Printer mein paper phans gaya hai. Colleague ko English mein batana hai.
Say: "The paper is stuck in the printer." If you want help, add: "Could you take a look?"
Mail mein likha tha "Please revert back." Back kyun likha hai?
"Revert" already means to go back, so "revert back" says the same thing twice. In many offices in India it is used to mean "reply". The clearest choice is simply: "Please reply."
My hair are very long. What is wrong?
The correct sentence is: "My hair is very long." Why: "hair" is a singular uncountable noun in English, so it takes "is".
Mehmaan ko bolna hai "Aap khaana khaake jaiye." Kaise bolun?
Say: "Please have something to eat before you go." It is warm and polite.
"Kya tumne apna kaam khatam kar liya?" English mein?
It is: "Have you finished your work?" In casual talk, "Did you finish your work?" is also fine.
"Mujhe ek minute do." Polite aur casual dono mein bolo.
Polite: "Could you give me a minute, please?" Casual: "Hold on a sec."
Bench par jagah dikhti hai. Pooch kar baithna hai. Kaise bolun?
Say: "Is this seat taken?" or "Is anyone sitting here?"
Agar wo mana kar de to kya bolun?
Say: "Oh, sorry. Thanks anyway." It is short and friendly.
Mere sentence mein kya galat hai? "Both of my sisters is married."
The correct sentence is: "Both of my sisters are married." Why: "Both of my sisters" is plural, so the verb is "are".
Meri cooking pe foreigner dost ne bola "Not bad." Kya ye taareef thi?
Yes, usually. "Not bad" means "quite good", but it is mild praise, not very strong praise. If the person smiled, it was a compliment.
Auto wale ko bolna hai "Yahin roko." Kaise bolun?
Say: "Please stop here." If you want the exact spot, say: "Stop right here, please."
"Mere paas ek bhi paisa nahi bacha." English mein kya kahenge?
It is: "I do not have even a single paisa left." In casual English people also say: "I'm completely broke."
Is it right? "Whose bag is this? It is mine's."
No. The correct sentence is: "It is mine." Why: "mine" is already possessive, so no "'s" is added.
Dost kehta hai "Don't take tension." Kya ye sahi English hai?
People understand it in India, but it is not the usual phrase in standard English. Say: "Don't worry" or "Don't stress about it."
Behen ka kal exam hai. Use good luck kaise bolun?
Say: "Good luck with your exam tomorrow!" Another short option is: "All the best!"
"Mere dada ji roz subah park mein tahalte hain." Translate.
It is: "My grandfather walks in the park every morning." In English, "grandfather" is the usual word, and "grandpa" is casual.
Aur dadi ke liye?
Use "grandmother" for the polite form and "grandma" for the casual one.
Aur nana-nani?
They are also "grandfather" and "grandmother". English does not separate the mother's side from the father's side.
Kisi ko mana karna hai: "Nahi, mujhe nahi chahiye." Polite aur casual?
Polite: "No, thank you. I'm fine." Casual: "Nah, I'm good."
"She is good at singing." Is it correct?
Yes, it is correct. "Good at" is followed by a noun or an -ing form, so "singing" fits well.
Aur "She is good in singing"?
That is not standard. We say "good at" for skills.
Maine veg order kiya tha, par ye dish veg nahi lag rahi. Waiter ko kaise bolun?
Say: "I ordered the vegetarian dish, but this one does not look vegetarian. Could you please check?"
"Bachche so rahe hain, dheere bolo." Translate karo.
It is: "The children are sleeping. Please speak softly."
Main bolta hoon "Wait, I am coming." Foreigner ko ajeeb kyun lagta hai?
In India it often means "I will be there soon". In other places "I am coming" sounds like you are already on your way, or it can sound odd. Say: "I'll be right there" or "I'll be right back."
He has bought a new shoes. Is this fine?
No. The correct sentence is: "He has bought new shoes" or "He has bought a new pair of shoes." Why: "shoes" is plural, and "a" can only go with one thing.
Pair ki jagah kya "a new shoe" bolein?
No, "a new shoe" means only one shoe. Use "a pair of shoes" for both.
Padosi se seedhi maangni hai. Kya bolun?
Say: "Could I borrow your ladder for a little while? I will return it today." "Borrow" means you take something and give it back.
"Wo baat karte karte so gaya." English mein bolo.
It is: "He fell asleep while talking."
"Zara meri baat sunna." Polite aur casual?
Polite: "Excuse me, could I have a word with you?" Casual: "Hey, got a minute?"
She is the taller in her class. Correct please.
The correct sentence is: "She is the tallest in her class." Why: when one person is compared with a whole group, we use the superlative "the tallest".
Party mein kisi ko apna parichay dena hai: "Main Neha ki dost hoon." English?
Say: "Hi, I'm Neha's friend." You can add your name: "I'm Priya, Neha's friend."
"Kal ki party mein bahut maza aaya." Translate.
It is: "I had a lot of fun at the party yesterday."
Form pe "Updation of address" likha tha. Kya ye sahi English hai?
"Updation" is used in India, but outside India people say "update". A clearer form heading is: "Address update" or "Update your address".
I can able to swim. What is wrong?
The correct sentence is: "I can swim" or "I am able to swim." Why: "can" already means "be able to", so "can able to" says the same thing twice.
Line mein khade hain. Dost se bolna hai ki meri jagah rakhna, main abhi aata hoon.
Say: "Could you please hold my place in the line? I'll be right back."
"Mujhe chhutti chahiye thi par mili nahi." Translate.
It is: "I wanted leave, but I did not get it." The word "leave" here means permission to be absent from work. In casual speech, people say "day off".
Room mein ek aur takiya chahiye. Reception ko phone pe kya bolun?
Say: "Hello, this is room number so-and-so. Could you please send one more pillow to my room?" Use your real room number in place of "so-and-so".
"Chalo, ab nikalte hain, nahi to train chhoot jayegi." English mein?
It is: "Let's leave now, or we will miss the train." "Miss" here means to arrive too late for it.
How much money you have? Fix this.
The correct sentence is: "How much money do you have?" Why: a question needs the helper "do" before the subject: "do you have".
Mera dost bolta hai "Where do you stay?" Iska matlab kya hai?
Usually it means "Where do you live?" But some people may think you are asking where you are staying at the moment, like in a hotel. To be clear, say: "Where do you live?"
"Mujhe lift de do" polite aur casual mein kaise bolun?
Polite: "Could you give me a lift, please?" Casual: "Can you drop me on the way?"
Packet par expiry date nahi dikh rahi. Shopkeeper se kaise poochun?
Say: "I cannot see the expiry date on this packet. Could you show me where it is?"
Is line ko English mein batao: "Mujhe nahi lagta ki wo aayega."
It is: "I don't think he will come." In English we put the "not" in the first part: "I don't think", not "I think he will not come".
She asked me to not to go. Please correct.
The correct sentence is: "She asked me not to go." Why: after "asked me", "not to" comes before the verb and "to" is not repeated.
To "to not go" bolna galat hai?
It is understood, and some people use it, but "not to go" is the usual and safer form.
Mail ke shuru mein "Greetings of the day" likhna theek rahega kya?
It is polite but old fashioned. Most modern emails begin with "Hello Ms. Rao," or "Dear Mr. Khan," or "Hi Anita," depending on how well you know the person.
Customer se kehna hai "Thoda ruko, main chhutta laata hoon." English?
Say: "Please wait a moment. I will get some change."
"Ye kitaab kal tak lauta dena." Translate karo.
It is: "Please return this book by tomorrow."
"By tomorrow" aur "till tomorrow" mein kya farak hai?
"By tomorrow" means no later than tomorrow. "Till tomorrow" means up to tomorrow and then stop, so it fits an activity that goes on, like "I will stay here till tomorrow."
Ye line sahi hai kya? "The reason is because he was late."
No, it is better to change it. Write: "The reason is that he was late." Why: "reason" already gives the cause, so "because" repeats it. Use "that" instead.
"Aap yahin ruko" - polite aur casual?
Polite: "Could you wait here for a moment, please?" Casual: "Wait here, okay?"
Dawat mein khaana bahut achha laga. Host ko English mein kaise bolun?
Say: "The food was delicious. Thank you so much for having us." It is warm and suitable for any host.
"Wo mujhse do saal bada hai." English mein likhna hai.
It is: "He is two years older than me."
I forgot mine pen at home. Sahi hai kya?
No. The correct sentence is: "I forgot my pen at home." Why: "mine" stands alone; before a noun we use "my".
Maine dost se kaha "I'll give you a missed call." Foreigner samajh nahi paya. Kya bolun?

A "missed call" is a call that rings and is not answered. In India people use it as a signal, but many foreigners do not know this habit. You can say: "I'll ring once and hang up, then you can call me back."
Teacher ne poocha "Samajh aaya?" Mujhe aadha hi samajh aaya. Kya bolun?
Say: "I understood some of it, but could you explain it once more, please?" It shows you are listening.
"Wo hamesha der se aata hai." Translate.
It is: "He always comes late." You can also say: "He is always late."
Nobody know the answer. Correct it please.
The correct sentence is: "Nobody knows the answer." Why: "nobody" is singular, so the verb takes -s: "knows".
"Mera intezaar mat karna" ko polite aur casual mein kaise kahun?
Polite: "Please don't wait for me." Casual: "Go ahead without me."
Teacher ko bolna hai ki mujhe sir dard hai, ghar jaane doge kya? English?
Say: "I have a headache. May I go home, please?"
"Wo mujhe dekh kar muskuraya." Translate karo.
It is: "He smiled when he saw me."
"He smiled at me" bhi chalega?
Yes. "He smiled at me" means the smile was meant for you. It does not give the time, so keep "when he saw me" if the time matters.
Aur "smiled to me"?
No. We say "smile at" a person, not "smile to".
Spelling check: "I did not recieve your mail." Right?
No. The correct spelling is "receive". Why: the rule is "i before e, except after c", and "receive" comes after "c".
Foreigner ko bola "It costs five lakh." Wo samjha nahi.
A "lakh" is used in India, and many people elsewhere do not know the word. Five lakh means five hundred thousand. You can say: "It costs five hundred thousand rupees."
Teacher se poochna hai ki answer mein marks kyun kate. English?
Say: "Could you please tell me why I lost marks in this answer?"
Aur isko aur narmi se kaise bolun?
Begin with thanks: "Thank you for checking the paper. I would like to understand where I made a mistake."
"Tumhari wajah se hi main pass hua." English?
It is: "I passed only because of you." A warmer way is: "I could not have passed without you."
"Mujhe bhi saath le chalo." Polite aur casual?
Polite: "May I come along with you?" Casual: "Can I tag along?"
Newspaper wale ko bolna hai ki kal se paper mat daalo, hum bahar jaa rahe hain.
Say: "Please stop the newspaper from tomorrow. We will be away."
We reached at the station on time. Is it correct?
No. The correct sentence is: "We reached the station on time." Why: "reach" takes its object directly, so no "at" is needed.
"Isse achha hota ki hum ghar pe hi rehte." Translate.
It is: "It would have been better if we had stayed at home." We use "would have" and "had" because we are talking about something that did not happen.
Dost ne bola "Same to same!" Kya ye sahi hai?
It is common in India, but it is not standard English. When someone wishes you well, say "You too!" or "Same to you."
Dukaan mein bolna hai "Mujhe ye wali nahi, doosri wali chahiye."
Say: "I don't want this one. I would like the other one, please."
"Hum sab ek saath khaana khaate hain." English?
It is: "We all eat together."
Every students must bring ID card. Please correct.
The correct sentence is: "Every student must bring an ID card." Why: "every" goes with a singular noun, and "ID card" takes "an" because "ID" starts with a vowel sound.
To "All students" sahi hoga?
Yes. "All students must bring an ID card" is correct, because "all" goes with a plural noun.
"Kitne baje milna hai?" polite aur casual mein?
Polite: "What time would suit you?" Casual: "So, when are we meeting?"
Bachche ko seat belt lagane ke liye kya bolun?
Say: "Please put on your seat belt." For a small child you can say it more gently: "Let's put on your seat belt."
"Mujhe ye kaam aaj hi khatam karna hai." English mein?
It is: "I have to finish this work today." If you want to stress it, say: "I have to finish this work today itself."
I have no any money. What is wrong?
The correct sentence is: "I have no money" or "I don't have any money." Why: "no" already makes the sentence negative, so "any" is not added after it.
Kisi ne poocha kaise ho, maine bola "I am fine only." Wo hans pada.
In India "only" is often added for softness or emphasis, but elsewhere it sounds odd. Just say: "I'm fine, thanks."
Dosto ke saath bill barabar baantna hai. English mein kya bolun?
Say: "Let's split the bill equally."
"Usne mujhe galat number diya." English mein?
It is: "He gave me the wrong number."
Madad ke baad "Aapka bahut shukriya" ko formal aur casual mein kaise kahun?
Formal: "Thank you very much for your help. I really appreciate it." Casual: "Thanks a lot!"
I am afraid of dark. Please check.
The correct sentence is: "I am afraid of the dark." Why: "the dark" is a fixed phrase that needs "the".
Dost ko bolna hai ki abhi busy hoon, baad mein call karunga. English?
Say: "I'm busy right now. Can I call you back later?"
"Subah se maine kuch nahi khaya." Translate.
It is: "I have not eaten anything since morning."
Maine email mein likha "Kindly don't mind." Kya ye theek hai?
It sounds odd to most English readers. Better choices are: "I hope you don't mind" or "Sorry if this is a bother."
Party mein pati ka parichay dena hai. "Ye mere pati hain." English?
Say: "This is my husband, Raj." Replace "Raj" with his name.
"Aaj mujhe kuch bhi achha nahi lag raha." Translate.
It is: "Nothing feels good today."
Kisi ko batana ho to kaise bolun?
You can say: "I'm feeling a bit low today." It is simple and honest.
I think so he will come. Is it okay?
No. The correct sentence is: "I think he will come." Why: "I think so" is a short answer on its own; before a full clause we say just "I think".
Dost ka exam kharab gaya hai. Use "Koi baat nahi, agli baar ho jayega" English mein kaise bolun?
Say: "Never mind, you'll do better next time." It is kind and short.
"Maine kabhi aisa nahi socha tha." Translate karo.
It is: "I had never thought of it that way." "Had never thought" refers to the time before you realised it.
The teacher explained us the lesson. Please fix.
The correct sentence is: "The teacher explained the lesson to us." Why: "explain" needs "to" before the person.
Ghar pe bijli gayi to maine bola "Current is gone." Kya ye sahi hai?
People in India understand it, but standard English says: "The power is out" or "There is a power cut."
Aur bijli wapas aa jaaye to?
Say: "The power is back." Some people also say "The lights are back on."
"Mujhe batana" ko polite aur casual mein kaise bolun?
Polite: "Could you please let me know?" Casual: "Let me know."
Cab book ho gayi hai, paanch minute mein aa jayegi. Ye English mein kaise bolun?
Say: "The cab is booked. It will be here in five minutes."
"Meri baat to suno." English mein?
It is: "Please listen to me." If you want the person to hear you fully, say: "Please hear me out."
Can you borrow me your bike? What should I say instead?
Say: "Can you lend me your bike?" or "Can I borrow your bike?" Why: "borrow" means to take and "lend" means to give, so "borrow me" mixes them up.
Aur "Can I lend your bike?" kaisa hai?
That is wrong. The person who takes the bike "borrows", so the sentence should be "Can I borrow your bike?"
Train mein bag upar rakhne ke liye kisi se madad maangni hai.
Say: "Could you please help me put this bag on the upper shelf?"
"Wo kabhi jhooth nahi bolta." Translate.
It is: "He never tells lies." "He never lies" is also correct and a bit shorter.
I am used to wake up early. Is this fine?
No. The correct sentence is: "I am used to waking up early." Why: in "be used to", the word "to" is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing.
Bank ke notice mein "Kindly co-operate" likha tha. Kya ye rude hai?
No, it is not rude. It is a formal request. A friendlier line is: "Thank you for your cooperation."
Notice mein kaunsa zyada accha lagega?
For a general notice, "Thank you for your cooperation" sounds warmer, and "Kindly cooperate" sounds stricter.
"Ye kaise kaam karta hai batao" polite aur casual mein?
Polite: "Could you show me how this works, please?" Casual: "How does this thing work?"
Dost ne naya ghar liya hai. Badhai kaise doon?
Say: "Congratulations on your new home!" You can add: "I hope you will be very happy there."
"Is baar main fail nahi hounga." English?
It is: "I will not fail this time." You can also say: "I won't fail this time."
"I will go to sleep early today." Is it correct?
Yes, it is correct. "Go to sleep" is the usual phrase, and "will" is fine for a plan you have just decided.
Bachche ko bolna hai "Khilone sametkar rakho". English?
Say: "Please put your toys away." For a young child, "Let's put the toys away" is gentler.
"Isko kaise kholte hain?" English mein?
It is: "How do I open this?" If you are asking about the usual way, say: "How does this open?"
Maine apne chacha ke baare mein bola "He is a very simple man." Foreigner ko ye insult lagi.
In India "simple" can mean humble and down to earth. In English it can sound like "not clever". Say: "He is a humble, down-to-earth man" or "He is a very modest man."
Kisi ka naam yaad nahi aa raha. Kya bolun?
Say: "I'm sorry, I can't remember your name."
Dost ke saath casual tareeke se kaise bolun?
Say: "Sorry, your name just slipped my mind."
"Humne kal raat hi sab kuch tay kar liya tha." Translate karo.
It is: "We had settled everything just last night." "Had settled" shows it was already done before the time you are talking about.
I will go for shopping tomorrow. Please check.
The correct sentence is: "I will go shopping tomorrow." Why: activities after "go" take the -ing form directly: "go shopping", with no "for".
"Aap kahan se hain?" ko polite aur casual mein kaise puchun?
Polite: "Where are you from, if I may ask?" Casual: "So, where are you from?"
Dawat se jaldi jaana hai. Host ko kaise bolun?
Say: "I'm sorry, I have to leave early. Thank you so much for inviting me."
"Mujhe lagta hai tum galat ho." English?
It is: "I think you are wrong." A softer way is: "I think you may be mistaken."
The boy whom I met him was tall. Correct it.
The correct sentence is: "The boy whom I met was tall," or more simply, "The boy I met was tall." Why: "whom" already stands for the boy, so "him" repeats the object.
Bus mein bolna hai ki jab bazaar aaye to bata dena, mujhe wahin utarna hai.
Say: "Please let me know when we reach the market. I need to get off there."
Mere dost ne bola "Let's do combined study." Kya ye sahi English hai?
People will understand it, but it is not natural. Say: "Let's study together."
"Aap pehle jaiye" polite aur casual mein?
Polite: "Please, go ahead. After you." Casual: "You first!"
"Tum mujhse naraz to nahi ho na?" Translate.
It is: "You aren't angry with me, are you?" The small question at the end, "are you?", asks the other person to agree.
"My brother is older than I am." Is it wrong?
No, it is correct. "Older than I am" is the formal pattern, and "older than me" is also common in speech.
Mobile ka text bahut chhota hai. Dukaan mein kaise bolun ki ise bada karke dikhao?
Say: "I can't see this clearly. Could you make it bigger, please?"
"Wo apne aap hi sab kar leta hai." English?
It is: "He does everything by himself." "By himself" means without help from anyone.
Maine foreigner ko bola "I did my graduation in commerce." Wo confuse hua.
In India "graduation" means the degree. In many places it means the ceremony when the degree is given. Say: "I completed my bachelor's degree in commerce."
I have lost my keys. Have you seen it? Is this okay?
No. The correct sentence is: "I have lost my keys. Have you seen them?" Why: "keys" is plural, so the pronoun is "them".
Agar sirf ek chaabi kho gayi hoti?
Then say: "I have lost my key. Have you seen it?" One key takes "it".
Padosi ko sorry bolna hai ki kal raat ghar mein function tha, isliye shor hua.
Say: "I'm sorry about the noise last night. We had a function at home."
"Chhote bachche bahut jaldi seekhte hain." Translate.
It is: "Small children learn very quickly."
"Mujhe aapki salah chahiye" ko polite aur casual mein bolo.
Polite: "I would value your advice." Casual: "What do you think?"
I want to learns English. Fix it please.
The correct sentence is: "I want to learn English." Why: after "to", the verb stays in its base form, "learn".
Main receptionist hoon. Sahab meeting mein hon to caller ko kya bolun?
Say: "He is in a meeting right now. Can I take a message?"
"Yahan se station kitni door hai?" English?
It is: "How far is the station from here?"
Restaurant mein maine bola "Please give me parcel." Foreigner dost ne kaha ye alag hota hai.
In India "parcel" is used for food packed to take away. In many places people say: "Can I get this to go?" In British English, "takeaway" is also common.
"Bahut din ho gaye, milna chahiye" polite aur casual?
Polite: "It has been a long time. I would love to meet up." Casual: "We should catch up soon!"
He did a mistake in the test. What is the right word?
The correct sentence is: "He made a mistake in the test." Why: we "make" a mistake; we do not "do" one.
Chhote bhai ko pyaar se kaise bolun ki padhai pe dhyan de?
Say: "I care about you, so please give your studies a little more attention." It sounds kind, not angry.
"Dukaan band ho chuki thi." English mein?
It is: "The shop had already closed."
"The shop was closed" bhi chalega?
Yes. "Was closed" tells us the state when we arrived. "Had already closed" shows it closed before we came.
Aur "The shop is closed"?
That is for now. Use it when you are looking at the closed shop at this moment.
A friend wrote "Your very kind". Is it right?
No. It should be: "You're very kind." Why: "you're" means "you are", while "your" shows ownership.
Ye kaam samajh nahi aa raha. Kisi se madad kaise maangun?
Say: "I'm having trouble with this. Could you help me, please?"
"Tumne mujhe bataya kyun nahi?" Translate karo.
It is: "Why didn't you tell me?"
Dost ne bola "She is the topper of our class." Foreigner ko kaise samjhaun?
"Topper" is common in India, but many people elsewhere will not know it. Say: "She is the top student in our class" or "She came first in our class."
"Mujhe ye gaana bahut pasand hai, main ise roz sunta hoon." English mein likho.
It is: "I like this song a lot, and I listen to it every day."
Khaane ki table pe namak maangna hai. Kaise bolun?
Say: "Could you pass me the salt, please?"
Aur jab wo de de to?
Say: "Thank you." If it is a friend, "Thanks!" is enough.
She is wearing a beautiful cloth. Please check.
The correct sentence is: "She is wearing a beautiful dress." Why: "cloth" is the material, and a garment is a "dress".
Bachche ne bola "Tomorrow is off." Kya ye sahi English hai?
People in India understand it, but standard English says: "Tomorrow is a holiday" or "I have the day off tomorrow."
"Mujhe jaane do, der ho rahi hai" polite aur casual mein kaise bolun?
Polite: "I'm sorry, I really must go now. I'm getting late." Casual: "I have to go, I'm running late."
"Running late" ka matlab kya hai?
It means you are behind schedule and may not arrive on time.
"Ye chhoti si baat nahi hai." Translate.
It is: "This is not a small matter."
Delivery wale ko bolna hai ki ghanti mat bajao, bachcha so raha hai.
Say: "Please do not ring the bell. The child is sleeping."
He left the house without to say goodbye. What is wrong?
The correct sentence is: "He left the house without saying goodbye." Why: after a preposition like "without", the verb takes -ing.
Interview mein maine bola "I am a fresher." Kya foreign company mein samajh aayega?
"Fresher" is common in India, but it may confuse people elsewhere. Say: "I'm a recent graduate" or "I'm looking for my first job."
"Aaj mera mood nahi hai." English mein?
It is: "I'm not in the mood today."
Aur "Mera mood kharab hai"?
That is: "I'm in a bad mood."
Sir ne jo kaha wo likhna hai. Unse kaise bolun ki dobara bolein?
Say: "Sir, could you please repeat that so I can write it down?"
I didn't do nothing wrong. Is it right?
No. The correct sentence is: "I didn't do anything wrong." Why: "didn't" and "nothing" make a double negative, so use "anything".
"Dhyan se, ye toot sakta hai" polite aur casual?
Polite: "Please handle this carefully. It can break." Casual: "Careful, it might break!"
"Chaabi mere paas hai, tum chinta mat karo." Translate.
It is: "I have the key, so don't worry."
Mail mein likha tha "Thanks to your good self." Ye kaisa lagta hai?
"Your good self" is an old-fashioned phrase, and modern readers may find it odd. Write: "Thank you" or "Thank you for your help."
"Aaj thand kuch zyada hai." English mein?
It is: "It is a bit colder today."
Agar bahut zyada thand ho to?
Say: "It is very cold today."
She is taller as her sister. Correct it.
The correct sentence is: "She is taller than her sister." Why: after a comparative like "taller" we use "than".
Dost ka phone gum gaya hai. Hamdardi kaise jataun?
Say: "Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that. I hope you find it soon."
"Wo dukaan subah nau baje khulti hai." Translate karo.
It is: "That shop opens at nine in the morning."
Class ko shant karana hai. "Dhyan se suno" polite aur casual mein?
Polite: "May I have your attention, please?" Casual: "Listen up, everyone!"
Bachchon ke saath kaunsa theek hai?
With children, the casual one is fine if you say it in a friendly voice. Add "please" to keep it kind.
He is the one who broke the window, isn't it? Please check.
No. The correct sentence is: "He is the one who broke the window, isn't he?" Why: the tag repeats the subject with a pronoun and the same verb: "is ... isn't he".
Kisi ka visiting card maangna hai. Kya bolun?
Say: "Could I have your business card, please?"
"Mujhe baarish mein bheegna pasand hai." Translate.
It is: "I like getting wet in the rain."
Foreigner ko bola "I want lady finger and brinjal." Wo samjha nahi.
These names are used in India. In American English they are "okra" and "eggplant". In British English, brinjal is called "aubergine".
Teachers' Day pe teacher ko wish karna hai. Kya likhun?
Write: "Happy Teachers' Day! Thank you for teaching us."
Ek line aur chahiye jo dil se ho.
You could add: "You have helped me believe in myself."
Let us to go now. Please fix.
The correct sentence is: "Let us go now." Why: after "let us" the verb has no "to".
"Pehle sochna, phir bolna." Translate.
It is: "Think first, then speak."
"Aaj mere saath chalo" polite aur casual?
Polite: "Would you like to join me today?" Casual: "Want to come along?"
Dost chai daal raha hai. Use "Bas, itna hi kaafi hai" kaise bolun?
Say: "That's enough, thank you."
"Wo apne kaam mein bahut tez hai." English?
It is: "He is very quick at his work." You can also say: "He works very fast."
She prefers tea than coffee. Is this correct?
No. The correct sentence is: "She prefers tea to coffee." Why: "prefer" is followed by "to", not "than".
Maine bola "Wait, I'll cut the phone." Kya ye sahi hai?
It is understood in India, but the usual phrase is: "Wait, I'll hang up" or "I have to go now."
Aur call uthane ke liye?
Say "pick up" or "answer": "Please pick up the phone" or "I'll answer the call."
Beech mein bolna pad gaya. "Maaf kijiye" formal aur casual mein?
Formal: "I'm sorry to interrupt you." Casual: "Sorry, didn't mean to cut in."
"Ye mera pehla mauka hai." Translate karo.
It is: "This is my first chance."
Dost ko bolna hai ki doodh ubal gaya hai, jaldi aao.
Say: "The milk has boiled over! Please come quickly."
She go to college by walk. Please correct.
The correct sentence is: "She goes to college on foot." Why: the verb after "she" takes -s, and "on foot" is the usual phrase for walking.
Aur cycle ke liye "by cycle" kaisa hai?
"By bicycle" and "on a bicycle" are both correct. "By cycle" is understood but less common.
"Humein ek doosre ki madad karni chahiye." English?
It is: "We should help each other."
Maine bola "I gave my exam yesterday." Kya ye sahi hai?
"Give an exam" is often used in India, but standard English says: "I took my exam yesterday." British speakers also say "I sat my exam".
"Galti meri thi" formal aur casual mein kaise kahun?
Formal: "I apologise. It was my mistake." Casual: "Sorry, that was my fault."
Dost se bolna hai ki kal ke bajay parso milte hain. English mein?
Say: "Can we meet the day after tomorrow instead of tomorrow?"
My all friends are here. What is wrong?
The correct sentence is: "All my friends are here." Why: "all" comes before the possessive "my".
"Ye utna mushkil nahi hai jitna tum sochte ho." Translate.
It is: "This is not as difficult as you think."
Phone pe maine bola "Sorry, I didn't catch you." Kya ye theek hai?
It is understood, but the usual phrase is: "Sorry, I didn't catch that."
Agar bilkul sunai na de to?
Say: "Sorry, I can't hear you. Could you speak up, please?"
Dost ka music bahut tez hai. Kaise bolun ki thoda kam karo?
Say: "Could you turn the music down a little, please?"
There are many peoples in the hall. Fix it please.
The correct sentence is: "There are many people in the hall." Why: "people" is already plural, so it takes no -s.
"Aapka kaam kya hai?" English mein kya hoga?
It is: "What do you do?" You can also say: "What is your job?"
Aur "Aap kahan kaam karte hain?"
It is: "Where do you work?"
Aur "Kitne saal se?"
Say: "How long have you been working there?"
Kal test miss ho gaya. Ma'am se kaise poochun ki parso de sakta hoon kya?
Say: "Ma'am, I missed the test. May I take it the day after tomorrow, please?"
Kisi ko phone pe dheere baat karne ke liye bolna hai. Polite aur casual?
Polite: "Could you please speak a little more quietly?" Casual: "Keep it down, please."
Shall we go to cinema? Is it okay?
No, it needs a change. The better sentence is: "Shall we go to the cinema?" Why: "the cinema" takes "the" in this meaning.
"Aap meri baat ka bura mat maniye." English?
It is: "Please don't take offence at my words." In casual talk you can say: "Please don't take it badly."
Bakery mein bolna hai ki cake par naam likhna hai. English mein kaise kahun?
Say: "Could you please write a name on the cake?"
"Yeh seat meri hai" ko English mein kaise bolte hain?
It is: "This seat is mine." If you want to be softer, say: "I think this is my seat."
She don't like homework. Please correct.
She doesn't like homework. Why: With "she" the helper verb is "does", so "doesn't", not "don't".
Dadi ko bolna hai "Aap aaram kijiye, main kar leta hoon." English?
It is: "Please rest, I will do it." If you are a girl speaking, the English is the same.
Dukaan par discount maangna hai, polite way mein.
Say: "Is there any discount on this?" or "Could you give me a better price, please?" Both are polite and clear.
Meri mummy kehti hain "light chali gayi". English mein?
It is: "The power has gone" or "There is a power cut." Both are common in India.
Yesterday I have met my old friend at market. Fix it.
Yesterday I met my old friend at the market. Why: "Yesterday" is a finished time, so use the past simple "met", not "have met". Also use "the" before "market".
Boss ko email mein "Kal main chhutti par rahunga" likhna hai.
You can write: "I will be on leave tomorrow."
"Namak thoda kam hai" kaise bolun restaurant mein?
Say: "The food needs a little more salt." That is polite. Please do not say "no salt" because it means there is none at all.
Rickshaw wale se poochna hai ki station tak kitna lagega. English mein?
Ask: "How much will it cost to reach the station?" You can also ask: "What is the fare to the station?"
Mujhe phone par bolna hai "Aap thodi der baad call karenge?"
Say: "Could you please call me back in a little while?" It is polite and clear.
Result ke baad dost se kehna hai "Tum pass ho gaye, badhai ho!" English?
Say: "You passed! Congratulations!" We write "Congratulations" with an s at the end when we use it as a wish.
I am studying in this school from 2019. Correct it please.

I have been studying in this school since 2019. Why: Use the present perfect continuous (have been studying) for something that began in the past and continues now, and use "since" with a starting point like 2019.
Padosi ke bachche bahut shor kar rahe hain. Unko politely kaise bolun?
Say: "Excuse me, the children are quite loud right now. Could you ask them to play a little quietly, please?"
"Sabzi taaza hai na?" English mein poochna hai.
Ask: "Are these vegetables fresh?" For one kind, say: "Is this spinach fresh?"
Diwali par dost ko wish karna hai. Short and sweet.
Write: "Happy Diwali! Wishing you light, joy and sweet moments with your family."
Meeting 5 minute late start hogi, team ko kaise batau?
Say: "The meeting will start five minutes late."
Bank mein bolna hai "Mera account kholna hai". English?
Say: "I would like to open an account, please." The word "open" is correct here.
"Kal match mein hum haar gaye" kaise kahte hain?
It is: "We lost the match yesterday." Remember: you win a match, and you lose a match.
Aur "hum jeet gaye"?
It is: "We won." You can add the match: "We won the match."
Ravi runs more faster than his brother. Can you fix?
Ravi runs faster than his brother. Why: "Faster" already means "more fast", so "more" is not needed.
Dukaandaar se bolna hai "Isse chhota size hai kya?"
Say: "Do you have this in a smaller size?"
Interview mein "Mujhe is kaam ka anubhav hai" kaise bolun?
Say: "I have experience in this work." If you want to give the time, say: "I have three years of experience in this work."
Garmi mein pasina bahut aata hai, ye "sweat" hai na? Sentence bana do.
Yes, "sweat" means the water that comes out of your skin when you are hot. For example: "I sweat a lot in the summer."
Mere papa ko bolna hai "Aap fikar mat kijiye." Kaise?
Say: "Please don't worry, Papa." It is gentle and respectful.
Teacher, I have a doubt. Is it okay?
It is understood in India, but in standard English "doubt" means you are not sure that something is true. To ask about something you did not understand, say: "I have a question."
Waiter ko bolna hai "Bill le aao." Polite English?
Say: "Could we have the bill, please?" In some places people also say "check", but "bill" is common in India.
Subah 6 baje uthna hai, dost se kehna hai "Mujhe jagana". English?
Say: "Please wake me up at six in the morning." The phrase is "wake me up".
"Mujhe gaana sunna pasand hai" ko English mein likho.
It is: "I like listening to music." You can also say: "I enjoy listening to songs."
Me and Priya is going for a walk. Is it right?
Priya and I are going for a walk. Why: "I" is the subject, so not "me", and two people need "are", not "is".
Reception par bolna hai "Mujhe doctor se milna hai". English?
Say: "I would like to see the doctor, please." If you have a booking, add: "I have an appointment."
"Hamare gaon mein bijli kam aati hai" kaise kahun?
Say: "We do not get much electricity in our village." Another way: "The power supply in our village is not good."
Galti se kisi ko call lag gayi aur woh uth gaya. Kya bolun?
Say: "I am sorry, I dialled the wrong number." Then end the call politely.
"Bhaiya, thoda side hona" kaise bolte hain? Bheed mein.
Say: "Excuse me, may I pass, please?" It is polite and works in a crowd.
Meri behen bolti hai "I am having a headache." Sahi hai kya?
It is not the usual form. Say: "I have a headache." Why: For pain or illness we normally use "have" in the simple present, not the continuous form.
Form mein "Father's name" ke neeche kya likhun agar papa nahi hain? English chahiye.
Write his name. If he is no longer alive, add "(late)" after it, for example "Rakesh Sharma (late)". If the form allows, you may also write "Not applicable".
Shop pe bolna hai "Yeh wapas kar sakte hain?" English?
Say: "Can I return this?" A more polite way: "Would it be possible to return this, please?"
Mummy ko bolna hai "Khana garam kar do." English?
Say: "Please heat up the food." In everyday speech "warm up the food" is also fine.
Professor se extension maangna hai assignment ke liye.
Write: "Dear Professor, could I please have an extension for the assignment? Thank you."
Conductor ko bolna hai "Mujhe agle stop par utarna hai".
Say: "I need to get off at the next stop." Another way: "Please tell me when we reach the next stop."
I am going to Delhi by flight yesterday.
I went to Delhi by flight yesterday. Why: "Yesterday" shows the past, so use the past simple "went", not "am going".
Mehmaan ke jaate waqt "Phir aaiyega" kaise bolte hain?
Say: "Please come again."
"Main der se pahuncha" ko English mein kaise kahenge?
Say: "I arrived late." If you are still on your way, say: "I will be late."
Homework complete hua ya nahi, ye "Maine homework kar liya" kaise bolte hain?
Say: "I have finished my homework." Or: "I have done my homework." Both are correct.
Dost ne kaha "Tu toh bada lucky nikla". Meaning kya hai?
He means: "You turned out to be very lucky." "Turned out" means that the result was a surprise.
Please revert back to me soon. Is it good English?
Not quite. Say: "Please reply to me soon." Why: "Revert" means to go back to an earlier state, so it is not the usual word for replying, and "back" repeats the idea.
"Thoda aur kam karo" bargaining mein bolna hai.
Say: "Could you reduce the price a little more?" Or: "Can you do a bit better?"
Mere dost ko khana pasand nahi aaya. "Mujhe yeh pasand nahi" politely bolna hai.
Say: "I don't really like this, but thank you." Or: "This is not to my taste, thank you." Both are polite.
"Seedha jaake left lena" kaise bolun?
Say: "Go straight and then turn left." If it is far you can say: "Keep going straight and take the first left."
"Aap hold karenge?" call par kaise bolun?
Say: "Could you please hold on for a moment?" or "Please wait a moment."
She have a new bike which are very fast.
She has a new bike which is very fast. Why: "She" takes "has", and "bike" is singular, so the verb is "is", not "are".
Mummy ne kaha "Dal mein tadka laga do." English mein kya bolte hain?
You can say: "Add the tempering to the dal." "Tempering" is the hot oil with spices that is poured over the dal.
Library mein book renew karwani hai. Kaise poochun?
Ask: "Could I renew this book, please?"
I have two sister and one brother.
I have two sisters and one brother. Why: After "two" the noun is plural, so "sisters".
Shaadi ke card par likhna hai "Aapki upasthiti hamare liye khushi ki baat hogi." English?
Write: "Your presence will bring us great joy." Another way: "We would be happy to have you with us."
Railway station par poochna hai "Platform number kya hai?" Politely.
Ask: "Excuse me, what is the platform number, please?"
Please give me a advice about my problem.
Please give me some advice about my problem. Why: "Advice" is uncountable, so it cannot take "a". Use "some" instead.
Naya fridge kharidna hai. Dukaan mein "Isme warranty kitne saal ki hai?" kaise poochun?
Ask: "How many years of warranty does this come with?" or "What is the warranty period?"
Colleague ko bolna hai "Aap mujhe file bhej dena." Polite email style.
Write: "Could you please send me the file when you get a chance?" The words "when you get a chance" make it softer.
"Chawal thode kam pake hain" ko English mein bolna hai.
Say: "The rice is a little undercooked." "Undercooked" means not cooked for long enough.
We played cricket in the ground. Is this correct?
Not quite. Say: "We played cricket on the ground." Why: We use "on" for a surface like a ground or field.
Mere padosi ne kaha "Please adjust kijiye." Iska matlab kya hai?
He means: "Please be flexible" or "Please manage with a small change." For example, he may want you to move a little so that he can sit or park.
Roz subah main walk par jaata hoon. "I go for a walk every morning" sahi hai na?
Yes, that is correct and natural. You can also say: "I walk every morning."
Mobile ka battery down ho gaya. English mein kya kahenge?
Say: "My phone battery has run out" or "My phone has died." For a low battery, say: "My battery is low."
Bank ke form mein "signature" ke bagal mein "date" likhna hai. Kaise likhte hain India mein?
Write the day, month and year, for example "15/08/2025". If you are not sure of the order, write the month as a word, such as "15 August 2025".
Mujhe kapde ka size chhota pad raha hai. Dukaan par kya bolun?
Say: "This is too small for me. Do you have a bigger size?"
Our guests are waiting since one hour. Please fix.
Our guests have been waiting for one hour. Why: Use the present perfect continuous for an action that is still going on, and "for" with a length of time. "Since" is used with a starting point.
Holi par rang lagane se pehle kisi se permission kaise maangun?
Say: "May I put some colour on you?" It is polite and lets the other person say yes or no.
Dukaandaar bola "Yeh last price hai". Iska kya matlab hai?
He means: "This is my final price. I will not lower it." You can then decide whether to buy or to leave.
The teacher gave us many homeworks.
The teacher gave us a lot of homework. Why: "Homework" is uncountable, so it has no plural "s", and "many" is used with countable nouns.
Application form mein "Marital status" kya hota hai?
It asks whether you are single, married, divorced or widowed. Choose the option that is true for you.
Boss se bolna hai "Mujhe aaj jaldi jaana hai." Kaise?
Say: "May I leave early today?" If you want to give a reason, add: "I have an appointment this afternoon."
Hospital ke bahar guard ko poochna hai ki visiting time kya hai.
Ask: "Excuse me, what are the visiting hours?"
I am afraid for the exam tomorrow.
I am afraid of the exam tomorrow. Why: We say "afraid of" for something that scares us. "Afraid for" means worried about someone's safety.
Waiter ko bolna hai "Yeh order mera nahi hai." English?
Say: "Excuse me, this is not what I ordered."
Dost ko bolna hai "Mujhe tumhari yaad aayegi." English mein?
Say: "I will miss you."
Mujhe ek line mein apna introduction dena hai: "Main Pune se hoon aur engineering padhta hoon."
Say: "I am from Pune and I study engineering."
Airport par bolna hai ki mera bag kaafi bhaari hai, kya extra lagega? English?
Ask: "My bag is a little heavy. Will there be an extra charge?"
Bijli ka bill zyada aaya hai. "Bill is more" likhun?
No. Say: "The electricity bill is high" or "The electricity bill is more than usual." Why: "More" needs something to compare with, so "is more" alone sounds incomplete.
Maine neighbour ko bola "You are a nuisance." Kya ye theek tha?
No, it is quite rude. "Nuisance" means a person or thing that keeps troubling you. A politer way is: "I am finding this difficult. Could we talk about it?"
Do you have a cheaper one? Is this good English?
Yes, that is correct and polite. You could also say: "Do you have something less expensive?"
Mujhe gitaar seekhni hai. "I want to learn guitar" ya "learn the guitar"?
Say: "I want to learn the guitar." With musical instruments we usually use "the" after "play" or "learn".
Bhai ko bolna hai "Meri help kar do." Natural English?
Say: "Can you help me?" Natural English does not usually say "do my help".
Bus mein ladies seat par baithna theek hai? English mein poochna hai.
Ask: "Excuse me, is it all right if I sit on this ladies' seat?"
Interview mein pooche "Tell me about your weakness." Kya bolun? Sirf language help chahiye.
A clear sentence is: "I sometimes take too long to finish my work because I want it to be perfect, but I am working on it." Change the content so that it is true for you.
"Mujhe yeh dikhana" kaise bolun dukaan mein?
Say: "Could you show me this one, please?"
Raat ko late soya, isliye aaj neend aa rahi hai. English?
Say: "I slept late last night, so I feel sleepy today." The phrase "went to bed late" is also good.
He is not agree to come with us. Fix it.
He does not agree to come with us. Why: "Agree" is a verb, not an adjective, so it takes "does not" and not "is not".
Team ko bolna hai "Kal tak report ready honi chahiye." Politely.
Say: "Could we have the report ready by tomorrow, please?"
Airport par poochna hai "Baggage kahan se milega?"
Ask: "Where can I collect my luggage?" or "Where is the baggage claim?"
Email ke end mein "Dhanyavaad" ke liye kya likhun?
You can write "Thank you" or "Thanks and regards". "Regards" is common for a work email.
Hamare yahan paani subah aata hai. English?
Say: "Water comes here in the morning" or "We get water in the morning."
She is having a good voice. Please fix.
She has a good voice. Why: "Have" meaning possession is not normally used in the continuous form.
Maine kal raat lights band karna bhool gaya. Sahi English?
Say: "I forgot to switch off the lights last night."
Tiffin mein roti aur sabzi hai. "In the tiffin" ya "inside tiffin"?
Say: "There are roti and sabzi in the tiffin." We normally say "in the tiffin".
Weekend par kya plan hai? Dost ko poochna hai.
Ask: "What are your plans for the weekend?" or "Are you doing anything this weekend?"
Message mein "Main busy hoon, baad mein baat karte hain" bhejna hai.
Write: "I am busy right now. Let's talk later."
Mehmaan khana kha ke gaye. "Thank you for coming" ke baad kya bolte hain?
You can say: "It was lovely to have you." If they brought a gift: "Thank you for the gift too."
This shirt is too much tight for me.
This shirt is too tight for me. Why: "Too" already means more than is right, so "much" is not added before the adjective.
Eid par dost ko message: "Eid Mubarak" ke saath kuch line likhni hai.
Write: "Eid Mubarak! I hope your day is full of happiness and good food."
Hostel warden ko bolna hai ki mera roommate raat ko late aata hai. Kaise bolun?
Say: "My roommate comes back late at night. I wanted to let you know."
Agar roommate ladki ho toh?
The sentence stays exactly the same, because "roommate" is used for both boys and girls.
Aur "at night" ya "in night"?
Say "at night". It is a fixed phrase. With other parts of the day we say "in the morning", "in the afternoon" and "in the evening".
I did a mistake in my test.
I made a mistake in my test. Why: We say "make a mistake", not "do a mistake".
Chai mein adrak daalna hai. "Put ginger in the tea" sahi hai ya "add"?
Both are fine. "Add ginger to the tea" is a little more common in recipes. "Put ginger in the tea" is fine in speech.
Dost ko kehna hai "Chal, chai pe milte hain." English?
Say: "Let's meet for tea." Or more casually: "Let's grab a cup of tea."
Dukaan wale se bolna hai "Yeh kharab nikla, badal do." Polite aur casual dono batao.
Polite: "This item is faulty. Could you please exchange it?" Casual: "This one doesn't work. Can you swap it?"
Meeting mein bolna hai "Main aapki baat se sahmat nahi hoon, par sunna chahta hoon." English?
Say: "I don't fully agree with you, but I would like to hear your view."
Her father is a doctor and she want to become one too.
Her father is a doctor and she wants to become one too. Why: "She" is third person singular, so the verb "want" takes -s.
Hotel mein room ka check-out time poochna hai.
Ask: "What time is check-out, please?"
Raksha Bandhan par bhai ko message: "Tum hamesha meri raksha karna." English?
Write: "Please always protect me, brother. Happy Raksha Bandhan!" The verb "protect" means to keep someone safe.
Bartan dhone ke liye "wash the utensils" ya "wash the dishes"?
Both are fine. In India "utensils" is common; in many other places people say "dishes". Use either one.
Maine kaha "I will discuss about the project." Teacher ne roka. Kyun?
Because "discuss" already means "talk about", so "about" is not needed after it. Say: "I will discuss the project."
Dost ne voice note bheja, par awaaz nahi aayi. Kaise batau?
Say: "I could not hear your voice note. Can you send it again?"
Pass book update karwani hai. Counter par kya bolun?
Say: "I would like to update my passbook, please."
"Mujhe meetha pasand nahi" ko English mein likho.
It is: "I don't like sweet food." Another way: "I don't have a sweet tooth", which means you do not enjoy sweets much.
Dost ke birthday ke liye "Bahut saari shubhkamnayein" ka English?
Say: "Many happy returns of the day" or simply "Happy birthday! Best wishes to you."
She bought a two kilos of apples.
She bought two kilos of apples. Why: "A" goes with one thing, and "two kilos" is plural, so "a" is removed.
Aunty ne poocha "Beta, kaha ho?" Mujhe jawab dena hai "Main theek hoon."
Say: "I am fine, Aunty. Thank you for asking." If they asked where you are, say: "I am at home."
Mera paper accha nahi gaya. "My paper was not gone well" sahi hai?
No. Say: "My paper did not go well." Why: "Go well" is not used in the passive, so "was gone" is wrong. Use the past simple "did not go".
Shop mein bolna hai "Mujhe sirf dekhna hai." Kaise?
Say: "I am just looking, thank you." That is the polite phrase used in shops.
Match ke baad dost ko bolna hai "Tumne bahut accha khela." English?
Say: "You played really well."
Hamare gaon mein ek talab hai. "A pond is there in our village" sahi hai?
It is understood, but the natural form is: "There is a pond in our village." Why: In English we usually start with "There is" to say that something exists.
Waiter ko bolna hai "Please less spicy banana." English theek hai?
Not quite. Say: "Could you make it less spicy, please?" Why: "Banana" is a Hindi word; in English we use "make".
Sunday ko main late uthta hoon. "I wake up late in Sunday" sahi hai?
Say: "I wake up late on Sunday." Why: We use "on" with days of the week.
Dost ki video call par screen freeze ho gayi. Use kaise bataun?
Say: "Your screen has frozen."
Aaj baarish ka mausam hai. English?
Say: "It looks like rain today." If it is already raining, say: "It is raining."
Dada ji ko bolna hai "Aap dhyaan se chaliye." English?
Say: "Please walk carefully, Dada ji." The word "carefully" shows how you walk.
The boss told to me to finish the work.
The boss told me to finish the work. Why: "Tell" is followed directly by the person, with no "to".
Doctor ke paas appointment cancel karna hai. Phone par kaise bolun?
Say: "I would like to cancel my appointment, please."
Gaane ka matlab samajh nahi aaya. "Gaane ka arth" English mein?
It is: "the meaning of the song" or "what the song means". For the words, say "the lyrics".
Mehmaan ko bolna hai "Ghar jaisa samjhiye." Kaise?
Say: "Please make yourself at home."
Application form mein "Date of birth" kaise likhte hain? DD/MM/YYYY ka matlab?
It means day, month, year. For example, 5 March 2004 is written 05/03/2004. Always follow the order that the form shows.
Dost ko bolna hai "Tumhara kaam bahut accha hai." Do alag tareeke batao.
You can say: "Your work is very good." Or: "You have done a great job."
Email subject mein "Chhutti ki application" ke liye kya likhun?
Write: "Leave application" or "Request for leave". Add the dates if you can, for example "Leave application for 10 to 12 March".
Mera dost mujhse naraz hai. "He is angry on me" sahi hai?
Say: "He is angry with me." Why: We say "angry with" a person.
Bill par galat amount lagaya hai. Cashier ko kaise batau?
Say: "Excuse me, I think there is a mistake in the bill. Could you please check it?"
Metro mein "Mind the gap" ka matlab kya hai?
It means: "Be careful of the space between the train and the platform." It stops people from stepping into the gap.
Meri behen ghar pe hai. "My sister is at home" ya "in home"?
Say: "My sister is at home." Why: "At home" is a fixed phrase, so we do not say "in home".
Interview ke liye "Aap apne baare mein bataiye" ka jawab kaise shuru karun?
You can begin: "Thank you for the opportunity. My name is Ankit, and I have just completed my degree in commerce." Change the name and facts to match you.
Professor ko bolna hai "Please aap dobara samjha dijiye." Polite English?
Say: "Could you please explain that once more?"
Pahad par trip hai, dost ko bolna hai "Garam kapde le aana." English?
Say: "Please bring warm clothes."
What is the meaning of "to pull someone's leg"?
It means to tease someone in a joking way. For example: "Don't believe him, he is only pulling your leg."
Pongal par South Indian dost ko wish karna hai, ek chhota sa message.
Write: "Happy Pongal! Wishing you and your family a bright and sweet harvest festival."
Meri bhabhi ne poocha "Kya tumne kha liya?" Mujhe jawab dena hai "Haan, abhi khaaya."
Say: "Yes, I have just eaten."
My brother do his homework after dinner.
My brother does his homework after dinner. Why: "Brother" is third person singular, so "do" becomes "does".
Bus late hai. Dost ko message: "Bus aane mein der hai, tum chalo."
Write: "The bus is late. You go ahead."
Lift kharab hai, secretary ko complaint likhni hai. Ek line.
Write: "The lift in our building is not working. Please arrange for it to be repaired."
Mehmaan se pooch rahi hoon "Aur thoda lenge?" Kaise?
Ask: "Would you like some more?"
Please give me one kg sugar. Is it fine?
Not quite. Say: "Please give me one kilo of sugar." Why: Use "of" between a measure and the thing measured. "Kilo" is also the usual short form.
"Der se aaye" ko English mein kya bolte hain? Teacher ko sorry bolna hai.
Say: "Sorry for being late." Or: "I am sorry I am late."
Maine apne kamre mein kitabein arrange kari hain. English?
Say: "I have arranged the books in my room."
Bank mein ATM card kho gaya. Kya bolun?
Say: "I have lost my ATM card."
What you are doing in the library?
What are you doing in the library? Why: In a question the helper verb comes before the subject: "are you".
Their is no sugar in the kitchen.
There is no sugar in the kitchen. Why: "There" shows a place or that something exists. "Their" means belonging to them.
The dog wagged it's tail happily. Check the spelling please.
The dog wagged its tail happily. Why: "It's" means "it is". For possession we write "its" with no apostrophe.
Meri nani bahut kam sunti hain. Doctor ko nahi, bas ghar walon ko batana hai ki dheere bolein. English?
Say: "Nani cannot hear well, so please speak slowly."
I have much work today and few time.
I have a lot of work today and little time. Why: "Time" is uncountable, so use "little", not "few". "A lot of" is the natural choice in a positive sentence.
Taxi ko bolna hai "Yahan rok do." English?
Say: "Please stop here."
Mujhe subah jaldi uthne ki aadat nahi hai. English?
Say: "I am not used to waking up early." Why: After "be used to" we use the -ing form, so "waking", not "wake".
Aur "I used to wake up early" ka kya matlab hua?
It means that you woke up early in the past, but you do not do it now. For example: "I used to wake up at five when I was in school."
Waiter ne poocha "Anything else?" Mujhe "Bas itna hi" bolna hai.
Say: "That's all, thank you."
I didn't studied last night.
I didn't study last night. Why: After "didn't" use the base verb, because "did" already shows the past.
Dost ne bola "Call me when you are free." Mera jawab: "Main shaam ko call karunga."
Say: "I will call you in the evening."
Class mein sir ne pucha "Any questions?" Mujhe question poochna hai. Kaise shuru karun?
Say: "Sir, I have a question." If it is a woman teacher, say "Ma'am".
Dukaan par bolna hai "Ye mera size nahi hai, thoda bada chahiye." English?
Say: "This is not my size. I need a slightly bigger one."
Mere neighbour ne mujhe bola "Aaj aapko disturb kiya, sorry." Mujhe reply dena hai "Koi baat nahi."
Say: "That's all right" or "No problem at all."
Maine apni teacher ko ghar bulaya. "I invited my teacher at my home" theek hai?
Say: "I invited my teacher to my home." Why: We use "to" for inviting someone to a place.
Mujhe aaloo ki sabzi bahut pasand hai. Different tarah se kaise kahun?
You can say: "I love potato curry" or "Potato curry is my favourite."
Sabziwale ko bolna hai "Thodi dhaniya free dena." Polite?
Say: "Could you add a little coriander for free, please?"
Diwali ke baad "Diwali ke baad safai" ke liye English mein kya bolte hain?
Say: "cleaning after Diwali". For example: "We do the cleaning after Diwali."
It is raining from morning.
It has been raining since morning. Why: Use the present perfect continuous for an action that began in the past and is still going on, and "since" with a starting point.
Mere team ne finals mein jagah banayi. English?
Say: "My team reached the finals." Another way: "My team made it to the finals."
Maa bimar nahi hain, bas thaki hain. Padosi ko bolna hai "Maa thak gayi hain."
Say: "My mother is tired."
Manager ne email mein likha "Please keep me in the loop." Iska matlab kya hai?
It means: "Please keep telling me what is happening." The manager wants to know about the progress.
Dost ne likha "I will come tomorow." Is it right?
Not quite. It is: "I will come tomorrow." Why: "Tomorrow" is spelled with one m and a double r.
Meri dost bahut shy hai. "She is very shy" ke baad kya jod sakte hain?
You can add: "She does not talk much with new people, but she is very kind."
Bank ki line mein agar koi beech mein ghus jaye toh kya bolun?
Say: "Excuse me, the line starts there. Could you please join the end of it?"
Hospital mein kisi ke liye "Jaldi theek ho jao" card par likhna hai.
Write: "Get well soon." It is the usual phrase for a card.
Form mein "Mother tongue" aur "Language" mein kya fark hai?
"Mother tongue" is the first language you learned as a child. "Language" or "languages known" lists all the languages you can speak.
Do you know where is the station?
Do you know where the station is? Why: In an embedded question the word order is the same as in a statement, so "where the station is".
Cooker ki teen seeti aa gayi. English?
Say: "The cooker has whistled three times." Another way: "I heard three whistles from the cooker."
Mere phone ka screen toot gaya hai. English?
Say: "My phone screen is broken." The word "cracked" is used when it has only lines on it.
Mall mein poochna hai "Trial room kahan hai?"
Ask: "Where is the trial room?" In many countries it is called a "fitting room" or "changing room".
Tum mere se zyada tez ho. Ye "faster than me" bolenge ya "faster than I"?
Both are correct. "You are faster than me" is more common in everyday talk. "You are faster than I am" is more formal.
Mere dada kheti karte the. English?
Say: "My grandfather did farming" or "My grandfather was a farmer."
Professor ne kaha "Submit by Friday." Matlab kya hai? "By" ya "until"?
"By Friday" means on or before Friday. It does not mean after Friday. "Until Friday" is used for something that continues up to Friday, so it is not the right word here.
Aunty ko "Aap kaise hain?" bolna hai. English mein kya kahun?
Say: "How are you, Aunty?"
Meri train 9 baje ki hai, isliye mujhe jaldi nikalna hoga. English?
Say: "My train is at nine o'clock, so I have to leave early."
Concert ke liye ticket book karna hai. Dost ko message likhna hai.
Write: "Shall I book the concert tickets?"
I am having a lot of friends in my class.
I have a lot of friends in my class. Why: "Have" meaning possession is not normally used in the continuous form.
Maine apna paper dubara check kiya. "I rechecked my paper" sahi hai?
Yes, "I rechecked my paper" is correct. You can also say: "I checked my paper again."
Maine mummy ko call kari. "I called to my mother" likh diya. Fix?
I called my mother. Why: "Call" takes the person directly, with no "to".
Teacher: "Write the essay in 100 words." Mujhe poochna hai "Kitne words tak?" kaise bolun?
Ask: "Up to how many words may I write?"
Dukaan wale ne bola "Aap bhaari discount ka faayda uthaye." Kya ye English theek hai?
Use: "Take advantage of the big discount." Note that the usual phrase is "take advantage of" for using a good chance.
Meri behen vegetarian hai. Restaurant mein kaise bataun?
Say: "My sister is vegetarian. Which dishes have no meat or fish?"
Kisi ko "tum" ki jagah "aap" kehne ka English kya hota hai? Respectful tareeka?
English uses "you" for everyone. To be respectful, use titles and words like "sir", "madam", "please" and "would you". For example: "Would you like some tea, sir?"
Dost ne kaha "Pack your bags." Mera matlab "Maine bag pack kar liya" hai. English?
Say: "I have packed my bag."
Hostel ka khana kaisa hai, dost ne poocha. Jawab: "Theek-thaak hai, par roz ek jaisa hota hai."
Say: "It is okay, but it is the same every day."
She is very good in cooking.
She is very good at cooking. Why: We say "good at" a skill.
Dost ko thank you bolna hai kyunki usne meri help ki. Kuch alag tarah se.
You can say: "Thanks a lot for helping me. I really appreciate it."
Bus mein bag seat ke neeche rakhna hai. Kisi se kaise poochun?
Ask: "Excuse me, may I keep my bag under the seat?"
Which one is correct: "He gave me a advise" or "He gave me advice"?
"He gave me advice" is correct. Why: "Advice" is a noun and is uncountable, so it has no "a". "Advise" is a verb.
Mummy ko "Mujhe bhookh lagi hai" bolna hai. Aur "I am hungry" ke alawa kuch?
You can say: "I feel hungry" or "I could eat something." Both mean you want food.
Boss ko email mein likhna hai "Mujhe kal chhutti chahiye." Polite English kaise hogi?
Write: "I would like to request leave for tomorrow."
The women is waiting outside the gate.

The women are waiting outside the gate.
Why: "Women" is the plural of "woman", so the verb must be plural: "are", not "is".
Sabziwale se poochna hai "Yeh tamatar kaise diye?" English mein kya bolun?
Ask: "How much are these tomatoes?"
Bus ka wait kar raha hoon. "I am waiting the bus from one hour" bola, sahi hai?

No. Say: "I have been waiting for the bus for one hour."
Why: "Wait" needs "for" before the thing you wait for, and "for one hour" gives the length of time. "Have been waiting" shows the waiting started in the past and is still going on.
Mujhe network nahi mil raha. Dost ko kaise bataun?
Say: "I am not getting any network signal."
Dukaan par poochna hai "Kya aapke paas isse bada size hai?" English?
Ask: "Do you have a bigger size than this?"
Aur "Yeh mujhe fit nahi aata" ko kaise kahun?
Say: "This does not fit me."
How many time will the journey take?

How much time will the journey take?
Why: "Time" is uncountable, so we use "much", not "many". "Many" is for things you can count.
Restaurant mein ek table for four chahiye. Kaise bolun?
Say: "A table for four, please."
Aur paani maangna ho to kya bolun?
Say: "Could I have some water, please?"
Party mein maine dost se kaha "I was very boring." Woh hans pada. Kyun?

Say: "I was very bored."
Why: Your friend laughed because "I was very boring" means you are a dull person. Adjectives ending in -ed describe how you feel, and adjectives ending in -ing describe what causes the feeling.
Teacher ko bolna hai "Maine homework nahi kiya kyunki main bimar tha." English?
Say: "I did not do my homework because I was ill."
She is interested to learn Kathak dance.

She is interested in learning Kathak dance.
Why: "Interested" is followed by "in", and a verb after a preposition takes the -ing form.
Bahut garmi hai. English mein kaise bolun?
Say: "It is very hot today."
Aur "Garmi se pareshaan hoon" kaise bolte hain?
Say: "The heat is bothering me."
Bank mein bolna hai "Mera khata band karna hai." English?
Say: "I would like to close my account."
Tomorrow is holiday, so the shops will be closed.

Tomorrow is a holiday, so the shops will be closed.
Why: "Holiday" is a singular countable noun, so it needs the article "a" before it.
Diwali par dost ko wish karna hai "Aapko aur parivaar ko Diwali ki shubhkamnayein." English?
Write: "Happy Diwali to you and your family."
Aur "Mithai kha lo" ko kaise likhun?
Write: "Please have some sweets."
Cab driver ko bolna hai "AC thoda tez kar dijiye." English?
Say: "Please make the AC a little cooler."
She is married since 2020. Is this sentence okay?

She has been married since 2020.
Why: "Since" a point in time is used with the present perfect ("has been"), not the simple present "is".
Mummy ko bolna hai "Khana bahut swadisht bana hai." English?
Say: "The food is very tasty."
Kal exam hai aur mujhe dar lag raha hai. English?
Say: "I have an exam tomorrow and I am scared."
Landlord ko bolna hai "Nal se paani tapak raha hai." English?
Say: "The tap is dripping."
Aur "Kal tak theek kar dijiye" kaise bolun?
Say: "Please fix it by tomorrow."
Aur "Kitne din lagenge?" ko bhi batao.
Ask: "How many days will it take?"
Hurry up, otherwise you will missed the bus.

Hurry up, otherwise you will miss the bus.
Why: After "will", the verb stays in its base form, so "missed" becomes "miss".
Interview mein bolna hai "Mujhe yeh kaam karne ka experience hai." English?
Say: "I have experience doing this work."
She cannot to sing in front of people.

She cannot sing in front of people.
Why: A modal verb like "can" or "cannot" is followed by the base verb without "to".
Guests aaye hain, unhe bolna hai "Aaiye, baithiye." English?
Say: "Please come in and have a seat."
The price of vegetables have gone up this week.

The price of vegetables has gone up this week.
Why: The subject is "price", which is singular, so the verb is "has". "Vegetables" only belongs to "of vegetables".
Kisi se poochna hai "Yahan paas mein ATM kahan milega?" English mein?
Ask: "Where can I find an ATM near here?"
Train late hai. Dost ko message: "Train do ghante late hai." English?
Write: "The train is two hours late."
Aur "Platform kaunsa hai?" ko kaise poochun?
Ask: "Which platform is it?"
Cricket match mein hum jeet gaye. English?
Say: "We won the cricket match."
Kal ki baat ka mujhe bura lag gaya. English mein kaise kahun?
Say: "I felt bad about yesterday's talk."
Email ke end mein "Dhanyavaad aur shubh kamnayein" likhna hai. English?
Write: "Thank you and best wishes."
Shaadi ka invitation mila hai. Reply: "Hum zaroor aayenge." English?
Say: "We will definitely come."
Who's umbrella is this? It was near my door.

Whose umbrella is this? It was near my door.
Why: "Whose" asks about the owner. "Who's" is only the short form of "who is" or "who has".
Airport par bolna hai "Meri flight ka gate kahan hai?" English?
Ask: "Where is the gate for my flight?"
Roommate ko bolna hai "Light band kar do, mujhe neend aa rahi hai." English?
Say: "Please turn off the light. I am sleepy."
Aur "Thoda dheere baat karo" ko kaise kahun?
Say: "Please speak a bit more quietly."
Dost ki dress ki tareef karni hai "Yeh tumpar bahut suit karti hai." English?
Say: "This dress suits you very well."
Dada ji bolte hain "Hum gaon mein khet mein kaam karte the." English mein kaise bolein?
Say: "We used to work in the fields in the village."
Dost ko bolna hai "Main das minute mein pahunch raha hoon." English?
Say: "I will reach in ten minutes."
Kisi ko beech mein rokna hai politely: "Maaf kijiye, kya main kuch bol sakta hoon?" English?
Say: "Excuse me, may I say something?"
Cafe mein order karte time maine kaha "I want a tea." Sahi hai?

Say: "I would like a cup of tea."
Why: "I would like" sounds more polite than "I want" when you order. "Tea" is usually uncountable, so people say "a cup of tea".
Dost ko bolna hai "Mera phone ki battery khatam ho gayi." English?
Say: "My phone has run out of battery."
Holi par dost ne poocha "What are your plans?" Mujhe bolna hai "Hum ghar par rang khelenge." English?
Say: "We will play with colours at home."
Colours ki spelling British mein kya hai aur American mein?
British and Indian English spell it "colour". American English spells it "color".
Meeting 3 baje hai. "The meeting is on 3 o'clock" sahi hai?

No. Say: "The meeting is at 3 o'clock."
Why: We use "at" with clock times, not "on".
Neighbour ka bachcha bahut shor karta hai. Unse politely kehna hai "Kya aap bachche ko thoda shaant rakh sakte hain?" English?
Say: "Could you please ask your child to be a little quieter?"
Bank wale ne kaha "Please fill in the blanks." Iska kya matlab hai?
It means you should write the missing information in the empty spaces on the form.
Teacher ko bolna hai "Mere sar mein dard hai, kya main ghar jaun?" English?
Say: "I have a headache. May I go home?"
Form mein "Father's name" likha hai. Iska matlab kya hai?
It means the name of your father.
It was a three hours journey by train.

It was a three-hour journey by train.
Why: When "three hour" works as an adjective before a noun, it is joined with a hyphen and "hour" stays singular.
The children plays in the garden after school.

The children play in the garden after school.
Why: "Children" is a plural noun, so the verb has no -s: "play".
Maine email mein likha "Please answer to my question." Teacher ne kaha galat hai. Kyun?

Say: "Please answer my question."
Why: As a verb, "answer" takes its object directly, so it needs no "to".
Gift ke liye dost ko thank you bola. "I thanked to her for the gift" sahi hai?

No. Say: "I thanked her for the gift."
Why: "Thank" is followed directly by the person, without "to".
